span.label: Female rats emit more conditioned eyeblink responses than males in both the hippocampus-dependent trace version and the hippocampus-independent delay version of the task.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The direction of the sex difference reverses in fear conditioning: males acquire and express conditioned fear better than females.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: On the harder two-way active avoidance task females learn to escape within the first trials while males need many more, and some males never learn at all.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Removing the ovaries in adulthood abolishes the female advantage in eyeblink conditioning, showing the effect depends on circulating ovarian hormones.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The sex difference in eyeblink conditioning is absent before and during puberty and only appears in adulthood, so it cannot be explained by plasma estrogen levels alone.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Giving testosterone to newborn females impairs their adult classical conditioning to male-like levels, evidencing an organizational hormone effect.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In conditioned taste aversion acquisition does not differ by sex, but females extinguish the aversion faster, drinking the sweet solution again sooner and in larger amounts.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Uncontrollable stress makes male rats fail to escape shock in active avoidance (learned helplessness) while similarly stressed females continue to escape.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Because females learn trace eyeblink conditioning better, more of the newly born hippocampal cells survive in females than in males.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Castrating adult males improves their operant avoidance learning, implicating adult testosterone in the male deficit.
